newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRAGUE BOURSE TO FORCE OFF-MARKET TRADE DISCLOSURE.
newsitem.headline: PRAGUE BOURSE TO FORCE OFF-MARKET TRADE DISCLOSURE.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's (PSE) trading committee on Wednesday agreed to a new rule requiring all members of the bourse to post details on trades they conduct off the PSE, the committee's chairman said.
The chairman, Vladislav Pavlat told a news conference that the disclosure would require all trades conducted by bourse members to be posted on the PSE's real-time quotation system.
"All members will be required to announce on-bourse and off bourse trades in real-time," he said.

He said the details of how the disclosure system would work would be decided within the next 14 days but the rule would not take effect until an extraordinary meeting of the trading committee was called to approve the methods.
Pavlat said the public disclosure would include volume and price of the trades conducted.
There have been widespread calls by investors watching the Czech market for more transparency in the pricing of especially off-market trades, where a major portion of turnover is still recorded.
The PSE now says that off-market trades account for about 50 percent of Czech securities turnover compared to more than 80 percent in recent years.
Pavlat also said that the Czech investment fund RIF had been approved to be added to the bourse's continuous trading session beginning on December 2.
There are currently 10 equities and two bonds listed for trading on the PSE's continuous session.
Pavlat said he expected the two bonds soon to be pulled from continuous trading because of virtually non-existent activity in the debt instruments.
Most secondary Czech fixed income trading is done in direct trades conducted over the counter.
